title: A Hungry Organ
text: Why does your brain burn a fifth of your resting energy? Your brain is only about two percent of your body weight. Yet it uses roughly twenty percent of your resting energy.
nxt: That is a very expensive organ. So how did our ancestors afford it?

title: Drying Plains
text: To find out, travel to East Africa, a few million years ago. The climate was drying, and the great Rift Valley was deepening.
nxt: Rainforests broke into patches of woodland and savannah.

title: Standing Tall
text: Crossing tall grass on all fours leaves you blind to stalking predators.
nxt: Standing upright lifts your eyes above the grass, so you can spot danger far across the plain. It also frees your hands.

title: Sharp Edges
text: A broken river pebble has a sharp, glass-like edge. With it, you can slice meat from an abandoned carcass.
nxt: The oldest widely accepted stone tools, about two point six million years old, were found in Ethiopia.

title: Bone Marrow
text: And with a heavy stone, you can smash tough long bones. Inside lies rich, fatty bone marrow that few other animals can reach.
nxt: That jackpot of dense calories could help pay for a bigger brain.

title: The Price of a Big Brain
text: A big brain is a hungry brain. Maintaining one demands a huge share of your daily energy.
nxt: That cost is much easier to pay with dense, nutritious food.

title: The Gift of Fire
text: Later, fire changed the menu again. Cooking over flames softens tough fibrous tubers and makes raw meat safer.
nxt: Many scientists suspect cooked food is easier to digest, freeing even more energy for developing minds.

title: Your Inheritance
text: Today, your brain holds about eighty-six billion nerve cells. And it relentlessly burns twenty percent of your resting energy.
nxt: You are carrying the metabolic legacy of stone-wielding survivors.
